newsitem.title: INDIA: Gold - Indian sub-continent prices seen rising.
newsitem.headline: Gold - Indian sub-continent prices seen rising.

text.p: Wedding season demand in India and political uncertainty in Pakistan are likely to push up gold demand and prices in the Indian sub-continent in the near term, dealers said on Monday.
Dealers in Bombay said demand for gold in India, the world's largest consumer of the metal, had stared picking up in the week to Monday when prices rose 20 rupees to 5,170 rupees per 10 grammes.
"A factor which helped the market firm had been the rising strength of the dollar against the Indian rupee," said Premchand Jain, vice-president of the Bombay Bullion Association.
"A costlier dollar has made gold imports dearer to that extent prompting prices to rise," Jain said.
Indian demand had earlier turned low after Diwali, the Hindu festival of lights, a little more than a week ago, when auspicious buying pushed up prices.
Dealers said a recovery in world gold prices had also aided local sentiment.
"Gold prices may look up further in the coming days," Jain said.

Dealers in Karachi, Pakistan's main commercial city, said bullion trade had been dull amid political and economic uncertainty following the dismissal of Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto's government on charges of corruption early this month.
They said gold consumption by jewellers had also increased due to the marriage season ahead of the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan due to start in mid-January.
In the week to Sunday, gold prices in Karachi rose 17 rupees to 5,315 rupees per 10 grammes.

Dealers in Dubai, the re-export market which supplies gold to the Indian sub-continent, said on Sunday they were hoping that India's wedding season will make up for poor jewellery and bullion sales during Diwali.

The second Indian marriage season, beginning mid-November and ending in February, usually sees a strong upturn in bullion and jewellery purchases, much of which is supplied from Dubai where prices are lower than in Bombay.
"We have to look now at the wedding buying," one Dubai souk (market) trader said.

Bullion imports into Dubai during this year's first Indian marriage season surged from 27.4 tonnes in March to 32.6 tonnes in April and 33.3 tonnes in May, the highest monthly import figures so far this year.
GOLD PRICES 24 CARATS PER 10 GRAMMES IN U.S. DOLLARS
(Conversion 1$=35.77 Indian rupees, 40.22 Pakistani rupees and 3.67 UAE Dirhams)
* Bombay prices November 18 & 11, Karachi and Dubai prices November 17 & 10 respectively.
-- Dev Varam, Bombay newsroom +91-22-265 9000
